what: The devnet test of the chain encoder (D1 and D2) as data: every transaction, who signs it with which tool, what it moves, what the chain should answer and what the lead does if it does not. plan.mjs prints the tables and the command lines of plan.md from it; sign-device.mjs builds the device's calls from it; check.mjs judges the recorded results against it; record-step.mjs send-file sends a research signer step only when its bytes are the plan's (research-signed.mjs, from the step's call line here); record-step.mjs stop records the lead's stop by the rows of send_outcomes and stop_table here; at a research signer step with a signed copy it needs the signer's lab.accountReads whose next nonce equals the copy's (the node counts its pool), and the pane's already-sent is a reading that rules out cases c and d. A $NAME is a value below, DEVICE (the device key's account, from results.json accounts.device.public_key), or $step.Pallet.Event.field (a field of an event recorded for that step).

EXPLORER.decided: FLOP's explorer, read by explorer-reader.js in a tab on its own origin: the lead read the rerun's A6 and A5 there and both agree with the committed record (lead-measurements-2026-11-13.json measurements.explorer and measurements.explorer_answer_shape)

TOP_UP.why: the brief: a tenth of the escrow

MAX_DURATION_D2.decided: short, so T7 can be sent soon after T6: below the ack window, so the channel of T5 has timed out by the time T6 may be sent. No lower bound is stated in the 1014020 metadata (no constant and no error names one); the upper bound for an open the miner did not sign is MAX_UNCONSENTED

ENCLAVE_KEY.decided: 32 bytes of the lab's own choosing: the ASCII text imd-flop-d2-enclave-key-20261112. The pallet does not verify TEE provenance for the key (the doc comment of open_channel)

SETTLEMENT.decided: the plain class: CertificatePremium needs INT8 exact serving and a weight commitment (errors PremiumRequiresInt8Exact, PremiumRequiresWeightCommitment)

N_T3.decided: a new channel nonce: the earlier tests' channels stay on chain, and a channel id that exists fails with ChannelExists

N_T5.decided: a second new channel nonce, for the channel of T5, for the same reason as N_T3

CH_T3.why: the channel of T3, derived and not read from an event: blake2b-256("FLOP/COMPUTE_CHANNEL/ID" || 0x01 || genesis || agent || miner || u64 little endian nonce), the agent being the owner. The formula is FLOP's SDK 0.6.0 channelIdV1 as the lead read it, checked against the rerun's force_open (lead-measurements-2026-11-13.json measurements.channel_id_formula; plan.test.mjs derives the rerun's channel ids). It is shown for force_open only

CH_T5.why: the channel of T5, by the same formula as CH_T3. Not known: the formula is shown for force_open only; T5 shows it for open_channel or refutes it (record-step.mjs checks every channelId the explorer gives)

fund_rule.why: FUND must cover every device transaction at the rerun's largest recorded fee, twice over: the fees of T4 and T5 are not known, and open_channel is 33 bytes longer than force_open. The rerun's FUND is used again rather than a new sum

node_codes_source: The node codes of the rows for refused-at-submission (1010 invalid, 1013 already imported, 1014 priority too low) are from the lead's knowledge of Substrate's author RPC. No committed file of this repo shows them. The first real refusal shows the shape of the node's answer (the runner keeps it as node: { code, message, data }).

send_outcomes.known: the extrinsic is in a block the node reported finalized, with the block's hash, number and the extrinsic's index, and the sha256 and length of that block's System.Events
send_outcomes.lead: record-step.mjs step --sent; then explorer.read and record-step.mjs step --explorer. plan.mjs next says what follows
send_outcomes.second_copy: never

send_outcomes.known: the node said finalized for a block that does not hold the extrinsic. Not known whether another block holds it
send_outcomes.lead: record nothing as included. lab.find from the birth block (mortal) or from the start of the run (immortal), and record what it returns
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: only by S4, once find has read up to a finalized head above the last valid block without it. Immortal: never; lab.sendSame

send_outcomes.known: the finalized block's hash is not the block at its height. Not known where the extrinsic is
send_outcomes.lead: as finalized-not-found: lab.find, and record what it returns
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: only by S4, once find has read up to a finalized head above the last valid block without it. Immortal: never; lab.sendSame

send_outcomes.known: the node said finalized, with the block's hash, but reading that block failed
send_outcomes.lead: lab.find from the birth block (mortal) or the start of the run (immortal): it reads the block again
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: only by S4, once find has read up to a finalized head above the last valid block without it. Immortal: never; lab.sendSame

send_outcomes.known: nothing was sent: the text or its sha256 changed on its way, or it holds no extrinsic
send_outcomes.lead: relay the send file and its sha256 again, exactly
send_outcomes.second_copy: not needed: the same copy is sent

send_outcomes.known: nothing was submitted by this call, but this page's sent list holds these bytes: they were written to a socket before (H2). It is a reading: record-step.mjs step records it, and nextOf takes the step as sent and not in a finalized block. It may be in the pool or in a block. With it in the record the lead's stop has neither case c nor case d
send_outcomes.lead: record it. Then lab.find from the birth block (mortal) or the start of the run (immortal), and record what it returns; if not found, lab.sendSame (immortal) or S4 (mortal)
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: only by S4. Immortal: never

send_outcomes.known: nothing was sent: sendSame sends only bytes send sent before
send_outcomes.lead: use lab.send
send_outcomes.second_copy: not needed

send_outcomes.known: nothing was written: the connection was not open. Nothing is marked as sent
send_outcomes.lead: paste the runner again in a fresh tab on the node, check its sha256, and lab.send the same send file
send_outcomes.second_copy: not needed: the same copy is sent

send_outcomes.known: on a first send: the node judged the extrinsic invalid (a bad signature, a used or future nonce it will not keep, a mortal copy whose era is over, or a fee it cannot pay): it is not in the pool and cannot be included as it is, and nothing moved. On a sendSame after an outcome that may still land (deadline, connection-lost, ended), 1010 can mean the first copy is already in a block (its nonce is used)
send_outcomes.lead: record it. After a sendSame that followed a deadline, connection-lost or ended: lab.find before anything else, from the block before the first send. After a first send: for an immortal step this is case c of record-step.mjs stop, and the cleanup steps that apply follow; for a mortal step, once the finalized head is above its last valid block, case b, or a second copy by S4
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4, when the nonce rule holds. Immortal: never; the lead stops at the step instead

send_outcomes.known: already imported: the node holds these bytes in its pool. It IS in the pool and may be included
send_outcomes.lead: treat it as sent: record it, then lab.find from the birth block (mortal) or the start of the run (immortal). No stop by the lead: the copy can land
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4 only, once its era is over at a finalized head and find did not see it. Immortal: never

send_outcomes.known: the priority is too low: another transaction of the same signer and nonce is in the pool. A copy the record does not hold exists
send_outcomes.lead: stop signing and find out which transaction it is (lab.find from the birth block or the start of the run). S2e refuses every device step until the record holds what is on chain. No stop by the lead
send_outcomes.second_copy: never while the other is in the pool; the lead rules

send_outcomes.known: any other code: not in the pool, by the node's word
send_outcomes.lead: record it and read the node's words. lab.sendSame of the same bytes later; no stop by the lead (record-step.mjs stop allows case c only with 1010)
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4, when the nonce rule holds. Immortal: never; lab.sendSame

send_outcomes.known: no final status before the runner's deadline of 120 s. It may be in the pool, or in a block that is not final (in_block names it)
send_outcomes.lead: record it. lab.find from the birth block until the finalized head is above the last valid block (mortal), or until found (immortal). Sign no later step meanwhile
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4 only, once its era is over at a finalized head and find did not see it. Immortal: never; lab.sendSame

send_outcomes.known: the extrinsic was written, then the connection was lost. It may be in the pool or in a block
send_outcomes.lead: paste the runner again in a fresh tab, then as deadline
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4 only, once its era is over at a finalized head and find did not see it. Immortal: never; lab.sendSame

send_outcomes.known: another transaction with the same nonce took its place in the pool: a copy the record does not hold exists
send_outcomes.lead: stop signing. lab.find from the birth block for this copy; S2e refuses every device step until the record holds what is on chain
send_outcomes.second_copy: never: the nonce is used

send_outcomes.known: it was in a block that did not become final in time. It may still be finalized
send_outcomes.lead: lab.find from the birth block, as deadline
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4 only, once its era is over at a finalized head and find did not see it. Immortal: never; lab.sendSame

send_outcomes.known: the pool dropped it. Not in a block, as far as the node knows
send_outcomes.lead: lab.find from the birth block, as deadline
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4 once its era is over. Immortal: never; lab.sendSame

send_outcomes.known: the pool found it invalid (for example its nonce was used or its era is over)
send_outcomes.lead: lab.find from the birth block; read the record's nonce rule
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4 when the nonce rule holds. Immortal: never

send_outcomes.known: find read the finalized blocks of the range it names and the extrinsic is not in them. Above the range, not known
send_outcomes.lead: mortal: find again from the end of the range until the finalized head is above the last valid block. Immortal: lab.sendSame, then find again
send_outcomes.second_copy: mortal: by S4, once the finalized head is above the last valid block and the nonce rule holds. Immortal: never

send_outcomes.known: find did not finish before the runner's deadline (H10): it read the finalized blocks from its start to the block it names in to (none when to is null) and the extrinsic is not in them. Above that, not known
send_outcomes.lead: record it. lab.find again from the block after to (from the same start when to is null), and record what it returns
send_outcomes.second_copy: as not-found: mortal by S4 once the finalized head is above the last valid block and the nonce rule holds. Immortal: never
